text:
ashley: heads up — multiple multi-GPU jobs on g5-pool-usw2 are failing mid-run with NV_peer_reset + ibv send errors. started last night, looks like 1-2h into long training runs.

mark: ouch. any reproducible job ids / nodes?

ashley: job ids 8672 / 8690 / 8701. nodes nid-uw2-g5-43/44/47. failures look cross-node (allreduce stage). logs attached below.

luca: can you paste the ibv_devinfo + dmesg around the crash? also kernel and mlx driver?

ashley:
```
$ uname -a
Linux nid-uw2-g5-43 6.1.21 #1 SMP Tue Feb 20 12:01:01 UTC 2025 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
$ modinfo mlx5_core | grep -E "version|parm"
version: 5.10.48
$ ibv_devinfo -v
hca_id: mlx5_0
transport: InfiniBand (0)
FW version: 17.33.1050
```
Dmesg snippets right after failure:
```
[123456.789012] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5e: ERR: WQ overrun on SQ 0x3
[123456.789315] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5e: RX queue crash detected, recovery scheduled
[123456.789900] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:81:00): 79, pid 9982, GPU 0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[123457.001234] ib_core:  mlx5_0: IB event port active
```
```
$ ibv_rc_pingpong -d mlx5_0 -s 1024
connect failed: Transport endpoint is not connected (errno=107)
ibv_rc_pingpong: QP 0x3: send failed, WQE error
```

mark: interesting — RX queue crash + WQ overrun. are these nodes all in the same rack / TOR? could be switch side.

tara: i pulled switch counters for tor-uw2-15, there are spikes in RX discard and huge PFC pause depth on priority 3 around the same timestamps. also saw an MTU mismatch on one leaf (tor-uw2-16) - it was accepting 1500 only while we advertise jumbo 65520.

nv-debug: can you run `rdma link show` and `ibdev2netdev` on one of the affected hosts? want to see mapping and if RoCEv2 flowlabel hashing is enabled on the switch.

ashley: ran them quickly:
```
$ rdma link show
1: mlx5_0 port 1 mlx5_0_1 state up phys_port1
$ ibdev2netdev
mlx5_0 port 1 -> ens192
```

ashley: quick workaround i tried: set host MTU to 4096 (was 65520) and restarted job 8720 on nid-uw2-g5-44. that job completed the allreduce stage without disconnects. seems correlated with MTU size.

luca: that points at fragmentation / switch path MTU / jumbo handling for RoCEv2. another suspected vector is RoCEv2 flowlabel hash handling on our Juniper fabric — we pushed a switch update last week that enabled flowlabel hashing for ECMP. if flowlabel gets set inconsistently it can end up steering packets to different ECMP paths mid-flow. that + large MTU can hit hardware pathologies and overflow device WQs.

mark: did the firmware roll happen around the same time?

tara: yes — TORs in racks 14-16 got firmware 22.1.4 on 1939987000 (yesterday). counters jumped right after.

ashley: summary of impact: ~12% of nightly e2e training jobs failed/retried last night, extra GPU-hours burned ~120 GPU-hours so far.

nv-debug: steps i'd run next:
- reproduce with small two-node NCCL job using the same MTU and message sizes (we have a repro script in infra/tools/nccl-repro)
- collect mlx5 dev counters: `mlx5_devlink port show`, `ethtool -S ens192`
- test with host MTU 4096 vs 65520 to confirm
- toggle RoCEv2 flowlabel hashing (switch-side) if possible

luca: possible short-term mitigations: set host MTU to 4096 cluster-wide for g5-pool (low-risk), or pin multi-node jobs to nodes behind same TOR to avoid ECMP. long-term: push switch firmware rollback/patch and upstream mlx5 driver tune (there is a driver patch that tightens WQ watermark handling).

mark: can infra ops coordinate with network team to rollback or apply vendor patch? we need a mitigation window.

tara: opened ticket NET-6421 with juniper TAC, provided counters and timestamps. TAC acknowledged a known issue with flowlabel+jumbo+ECMP on that firmware family. they suggested disabling flowlabel hashing for RoCEv2 as immediate mitigation.

ashley: i applied host-MTU-to-4096 as a conservative cluster-level workaround around 1939994000 for affected pool; jobs stabilized. leaving it there until patch. posting runbook steps below.

ashley: RUNBOOK (workaround)
```
# on nodes in g5-pool-usw2
sudo ip link set dev ens192 mtu 4096
# restart kubelet / gpu-allocator if needed
sudo systemctl restart kubelet
```

luca: follow-ups / owner:
- NET: disable RoCEv2 flowlabel hashing on fabric (tara)
- INFRA: keep MTU 4096 until patch (mark)
- RUNTIME: validate mlx5 driver patch and schedule driver upgrade (luca)
- SRE: monitor job success rate & GPU-hours spent (sre-bot + ashley)

sre-bot: alert cleared for g5-pool-usw2 packet-loss spike. continuing to monitor 5m. :eyes:

ashley: note for postmortem: root cause appears to be interaction of switch firmware flowlabel ECMP hashing + jumbo MTU handing causing RX queue overruns on mlx5 NICs. vendor patch incoming; we will roll to prod after validation.

mark: thanks everyone. can we add a short note to infra-runbooks about MTU/rocev troubleshooting and the specific firmware versions to watch for?

ashley: already adding it to infra/runbooks/networking.md — will include the commands we ran and the mitigation checklist.

luca: triage done. will coordinate driver test tomorrow in staging and schedule vendor firmware update once TAC provides patch.

ashley: closing here — will post postmortem link when done. :thumbsup:
